name: Bark-Furnace
description: Bark-Furnace earns its name from its surface, which resembles the cracked, blackened bark of a tree consumed by fire. Tectonic plates grind and split with visible speed, revealing the molten orange interior beneath crusts of cooling basalt that form, fracture, and reform in a cycle measured in hours rather than millennia. Supervolcanoes dot the equatorial belt, their eruption plumes merging into a permanent canopy of ash and sulfur that blocks direct sunlight and paints the sky in shades of bruised orange.

The heat on Bark-Furnace is a physical force. Even in hardened survey craft, crews report the oppressive awareness of temperature pressing against every hull plate, and the toxic atmosphere carries particulates that abrade exposed sensors within days. The sound environment is dominated by the deep, irregular drumming of tectonic activity, punctuated by the explosive reports of volcanic detonations that propagate through the dense atmosphere as concussive waves. There is no silence here, only variations in violence.

Despite conditions that should preclude all biology, Bark-Furnace hosts a thriving community of extremophilic microorganisms that metabolize sulfur compounds and exotic matter deposits found near the exposed planetary core. These organisms have evolved biochemistries unknown elsewhere, incorporating exotic matter into their cellular structures in ways that defy current models. Their discovery has raised fundamental questions about the relationship between exotic matter and the origin of life.

Mining interests have claimed rights to Bark-Furnace's exotic matter deposits, but extraction in such an active tectonic environment has proven catastrophically difficult. Three automated mining installations have been destroyed by volcanic activity, and insurers now refuse coverage for surface operations. The microbial organisms, however, concentrate exotic matter in their biomass at rates far exceeding industrial processes, leading to proposals for bio-harvesting that raise their own ethical and practical challenges.
